# Review instructions

How Claude reviews a pull request in this repo (playbook Stage 5, "AI in the PR review loop"). Written by the tech lead (sample data:
Khoa). Findings are advisory: they never approve or block a pull request. A person approves.

Read first: the diff, `CLAUDE.md`, and the spec and plan the pull request names in `PR.md` (`spec/`, `plan/`). Read the policies in
`.claude/skills/policy-*/SKILL.md` when a change touches what they cover.

## Passes

Run three passes, in this order. Each finding belongs to exactly one pass.

1. **Bugs**: logic errors, wrong edge cases (empty list, filter active, one item, many items), state that is saved but not shown or shown
   but not saved, broken keyboard use.
2. **Security**: `policy-security`. User text reaches the page only through `textContent` (S3). Imported files are validated (S1). No new
   network request, script, CDN or dependency (S4). Nothing destructive without a confirm (S2).
3. **Compliance**: the change does what its accepted spec and plan say, and nothing the spec puts out of scope. UI text follows
   `policy-ux` (Vietnamese, short, no technical words). `CLAUDE.md` rules (size of change, tests with the fix).

## What Important means here

A finding is **Important** if it would break behaviour a user relies on, lose or leak data, or breach a policy or an accepted spec.
Everything else is a **Nit**: naming, formatting, comments, style, a cleaner way to write the same thing.

If you are not sure a problem is real, say what you would check, and mark it Nit.

## Cap the nits

At most **5 nits** per review. Pick the ones most worth a person's time. Say how many you dropped.

## Do not report

- Anything `bash scripts/check.sh` already checks (tests pass, syntax).
- `demo/`, `evals/results/`, `review/`: evidence and generated output.
- Wording inside `tickets/` and `docs/`: not working files.
- Praise, summaries of what the diff does, or restating the PR description.

## Also say

- If the change makes `CLAUDE.md` out of date (a command, a rule, a file it names), report it as a Compliance finding.
- If the same mistake is already listed under "Things Claude gets wrong" in `CLAUDE.md`, say so: the line is not working.

+# PR 9 · Quarantine the flaky random-title backup test
+
+Author: fx-sdlc-agent (watch job, ci_fail_rate level 3, simulated day 36 · 2026-11-05) · Status: waiting for a person's review
+
+## Why
+
+CI has failed 1–2 of 4 runs every day since day 31 (0.5 on days 35 and 36), always on the same test, "a list with random titles
+survives backup and import". `randomTitle()` in `tests/backup.test.js` can return `""` (`n = Math.floor(Math.random() * 12)`
+can be 0). The app never creates an empty title, and `parseBackup` is right to reject one (app/backup.js:66). So the test is wrong,
+not the app. All 9 failed runs (days 31–36) logged a `""` title. Full diagnosis:
+`intent/auto/2026-11-01-ci-random-titles-test-empty-title.md`.
+
+## What changes
+
+- `tests/backup.test.js`: the test gets `{ skip: 'quarantined: …' }` plus a comment. The test body and generator are **not** changed.
+- `CLAUDE.md`: the test is added to the "Flaky tests (quarantined)" line.
+
+I picked quarantine, not a revert of 9253a71. A revert would delete the test, and the test is good coverage once its generator is
+fixed. Fixing the generator (titles of length ≥ 1, not blank) changes a committed test. That is a person's decision (tech lead),
+so this PR does not do it.
+
+## Risk
+
+Low. No file under `app/` changes. Cost: backup round-trips with random titles are not covered until the skip is removed. The
+fixed round-trip test still runs.
+
+## Check (run on this branch, after the last change)
+
+```
+== test: node --test
+ℹ tests 47
+ℹ pass 46
+ℹ fail 0
+== lint: node --check app/*.js tests/*.js
+== check: OK
+```
+
+`tests` (47) ≠ `pass` (46) because one test is skipped on purpose. That is the quarantine.
+
+## For the reviewer
+
+- Tech lead: merge the quarantine as it is, or fix the generator in this PR instead (then drop the skip and the CLAUDE.md line)?
+- Follow-up: remove the skip and the CLAUDE.md line once the generator is fixed.
+
+🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

owner: Huy (on-call this week, simulated) · reviewed by Khoa (tech lead, simulated)

        rollback(env=staging), then confirm with python3 scripts/collect.py traffic --env staging --day <same day> --confirm

      6-9 happens a few times a year by chance alone.
    fixed:
      smooth: 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# One command for "is the work done": every test, then a syntax check of every script. Exit code is non-zero on any failure.
# Run as `bash scripts/check.sh` (do not rely on the executable bit: uploads can drop it).
set -u
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
fail=0
echo "== test: node --test"
node --test 2>&1 | grep -E '^(not ok|ℹ (tests|pass|fail))' || true
node --test >/dev/null 2>&1 || fail=1
echo "== lint: node --check app/*.js tests/*.js"
for f in app/*.js tests/*.js; do node --check "$f" || { echo "lint failed: $f"; fail=1; }; done
[ "$fail" = 0 ] && echo "== check: OK" || echo "== check: FAILED"
exit "$fail"
